primary_question: Does human-rated difficulty predict assisted exact first-move correctness within each deployment?
primary_regression: Separate statsmodels binomial GLM per model on all 1000 completed responses: success ~ const + (puzzle_rating-1500)/500 + indicator(total_solver_moves>1). No predictor selection or tuning.
primary_tests: Two prespecified rating-coefficient tests, with Holm-adjusted p-values across the two deployments. Report per-model odds ratios and ordinary 95% model-based intervals, labeled as unadjusted for multiplicity.
regression_gate: All 1000 unique planned puzzles have audited completed provider responses; at least 50 successes and 50 failures; converged finite fit with no separation. Otherwise descriptive results only.
tree_question: Can rating, solver-move count and legal-choice count predict first-move success on held-out puzzles?
tree: Numeric CART, Gini splits, max_depth=2, min_leaf=40, features=[puzzle_rating,total_solver_moves,legal_moves], fixed class threshold probability>=0.5. Fit on the 800 training puzzles only; no hyperparameter tuning or feature selection.
tree_gate: All 1000 outcomes audited; at least 30 training successes and 30 training failures. Test outcomes must not be used for fitting or tuning.
evaluation: Evaluate once on the 200 fixed held-out puzzles: accuracy with Wilson interval, balanced accuracy, ROC AUC when both classes exist, Brier score and confusion counts. Compare accuracy with the constant majority class chosen using training labels only.
holdout_policy: The 20-case operational check uses training rows only. I do not inspect holdout performance until collection and audits are complete. Any prompt/scoring/predictor change after new responses requires a separate version and sample; I do not reuse this holdout to tune.
missingness: I keep infrastructure failures pending and report attempted/completed counts; I do not code them as wrong answers or silently drop them to meet gates.
sampling_scope: Approximately equal allocation across six rating-by-length cells, not population-representative accuracy. Same positions and split for both models; no pooled independent-row model comparison.
sampling_exclusions: All previously exposed/reserved IDs found in historical sample/experiment CSVs, outcomes and exclusion metadata; prior solver positions; distinct solver position keys within the new sample.
inference_limitations: Position deduplication reduces exact duplicates but does not guarantee independence of games or themes; association is observational and legal-choice assistance limits generalization.
